result.message: Restores pre-6.1.0 collection behavior for symlinked directories. Removed `follow_symlinks=False` from `visit()` in src/_pytest/pathlib.py (introduced in b473e515bc57ff1133fe650f1e7e6d7e22e5d841 for 6.1.0). `entry.is_dir()` now follows directory symlinks so they are recursed into and collected as usual, matching the issue's requested fix. result.message:
Deliver this exact version (v4, patch-2, files_sha256 1208f7f7...).

Behavior change: in src/_pytest/pathlib.py `visit()`, `entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)` -> `entry.is_dir()`, so symlinks to directories are followed and collected instead of being skipped. This is exactly the removal requested by the issue (regression from b473e515bc57ff1133fe650f1e7e6d7e22e5d841 in 6.1.0). No other callers of `visit()` depend on the false-follow behavior; file symlinks were already collected (see existing test_collect_symlink_file_arg).

Verification on this exact version:
- New issue-specific regression test `testing/test_collection.py::test_collect_symlink_directory`, which builds `dir/test_real.py` + a `symlink_to_dir` symlink and asserts `symlink_to_dir/test_real.py::test_real` is actually collected and PASSED. Focused symlink run: 3 passed; the nested node view showed both `dir/test_real.py::test_real` and `symlink_to_dir/test_real.py::test_real` passing, directly proving the symlinked directory is collected.
- Broader: testing/test_pathlib.py + testing/test_collection.py — 142 collected, 141 passed, 1 xfailed, 0 failed, 0 errors.

Self-review correction: my first run (v2) passed only on unrelated suites and did not exercise the symlink-to-directory case; I added the regression test and initially mis-asserted a pass count, then fixed the assertion to match the real (2 passed) output. Remaining unverified: hidden acceptance, other OS/CI environments beyond this Linux testbed, and recursive symlink-loop/duplicate-collection edge cases which I did not test.
